before_manifest_row.title: Finite speed of propagation for linear symmetric hyperbolic systems: cone domination and independence of the extension
before_manifest_row.statement:
Let $T>0$, let $A^\mu:(-T,T)\times\mathbb R^3\to\operatorname{Sym}_m(\mathbb R)$
($\mu=0,1,2,3$) be smooth with $A^0(t,x)\ge aI$ for some constant $a>0$ and all
$(t,x)$, and let $\|A^i(t,x)\|\le b$ for the operator norm and all $i,t,x$. Let
$C:(-T,T)\times\mathbb R^3\to M_m(\mathbb R)$ be smooth and bounded by $K$.

**(a)** Put $\lambda:=\sqrt3\,b/a+1$; then $\lambda A^0(t,x)+\xi_iA^i(t,x)\ge0$ as a
quadratic form for every $(t,x)$ and every $\xi\in\mathbb R^3$ with
$|\xi|\le1$.

**(b)** Let $w\in C^1((-T,T)\times\mathbb R^3;\mathbb R^m)$ solve
$$A^0\partial_tw+A^i\partial_iw+Cw=0 ,$$
and let $x_0\in\mathbb R^3$, $0<t_0<T$, and suppose $w(0,x)=0$ for every
$|x-x_0|\le\lambda t_0$. Then $w(t,x)=0$ for every
$(t,x)\in\{(t,x):0\le t\le t_0,\ |x-x_0|\le\lambda(t_0-t)\}$.

**(c)** [independence of the extension] If $w_1,w_2$ are two solutions of two
such systems whose complete coefficient families, including $C$, agree on an open set containing the
truncated cone $D=\{(t,x):0\le t\le t_0,|x-x_0|\le\lambda(t_0-t)\}$, and if
$w_1(0,x)=w_2(0,x)$ for $|x-x_0|\le\lambda t_0$, then $w_1=w_2$ on $D$.

before_manifest_row.title: Compactness of H^r-bounded families in H^{r-1} and locally uniform H^{s-1} subsequences of Galerkin solutions
before_manifest_row.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]).

**(a)** For every integer $r\ge1$, every $R\ge0$ and every sequence $(v_j)$
in $H^r(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m)$ with $\|v_j\|_{H^r}\le R$ there is a
subsequence converging in $H^{r-1}(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m)$.

**(b)** Let $s\ge5$, $R\ge0$, $T>0$ with the compact slab $[-T,T]$ contained in the coefficient time domain $I$, let $K\subseteq O$ be compact, and let
$u_N:(-T,T)\to X_N$ ($N\in\mathcal N$), where $\mathcal N\subseteq\mathbb N_0$ is any infinite set of Fourier cutoffs be a family of Galerkin solutions with
$u_N(t)$ taking values in $K$ and $\|u_N(t)\|_{H^s}\le R$ for all $t$. Then the
family is equicontinuous in the $H^{s-1}$ metric: there is
$C_0=C_0(A^\mu,B,K,R,s,[-T,T])$ with
$$\|u_N(t)-u_N(t')\|_{H^{s-1}}\le C_0\,|t-t'|\qquad(t,t'\in(-T,T),\ N\in\mathcal N).$$

**(c)** Under the hypotheses of (b) there are a strictly increasing sequence
$N_j\in\mathcal N$, $N_j\to\infty$ and $u\in C^0((-T,T);H^{s-1}(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m))$
with $u_{N_j}\to u$ uniformly on every compact subinterval of $(-T,T)$ in the
$H^{s-1}$ norm.

before_manifest_row.title: Gauss-Codazzi decomposition in Gaussian normal coordinates and the constraint equations in terms of the induced metric and second fundamental form
before_manifest_row.statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold, and let $\Sigma\subseteq M$ be a smooth spacelike embedded hypersurface with future unit normal $n$, induced Riemannian metric $h$ and second fundamental form $K(X,Y)=g(\nabla_Xn,Y)$ ([[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]], [[lem-gr-spacelike-hypersurface-normal-and-second-fundamental-form]]). Write $D$ for the Levi-Civita connection of $h$, $R^h$ for its curvature operator in the same operator convention as the ambient curvature, and $S_h$ for its scalar curvature. Explicitly distinguish the lowered tensor from the operator pairing by setting
$$\mathcal R^g(A,B,C,D):=g(R^g(C,D)B,A),\qquad \mathcal R^h(A,B,C,D):=h(R^h(C,D)B,A).$$
Thus $\mathcal R^g_{abcd}=R_{abcd}$ in [[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]; in particular $g(R^g(X,Y)Z,W)=\mathcal R^g(W,Z,X,Y)$. Let $G$ be the Einstein tensor defined there. At every $p\in\Sigma$ and for all $X,Y,Z,W\in T_p\Sigma$:

**(a) Gauss equation.**
$$\mathcal R^g(X,Y,Z,W)=\mathcal R^h(X,Y,Z,W)+K(X,Z)K(Y,W)-K(X,W)K(Y,Z).$$
Equivalently, in operator order,
$$g(R^g(X,Y)Z,W)=h(R^h(X,Y)Z,W)+K(Y,Z)K(X,W)-K(X,Z)K(Y,W).$$

**(b) Codazzi equation.**
$$g(R^g(X,Y)Z,n)=(D_YK)(X,Z)-(D_XK)(Y,Z).$$

**(c) Normal projections.** Define $(\operatorname{div}_hK)(Y)=h^{ij}(D_{e_i}K)(e_j,Y)$, $\tau=\operatorname{tr}_hK=h^{ij}K_{ij}$ and $|K|_h^2=h^{ik}h^{jl}K_{ij}K_{kl}$. Then
$$G(n,n)=\tfrac12(S_h+\tau^2-|K|_h^2),\qquad G(n,Y)=(\operatorname{div}_hK)(Y)-D_Y\tau.$$

**(d) Constraint equations.** If the tensor equation $G+\Lambda g=\kappa T$ holds at $p$, for a smooth symmetric covariant $2$-tensor $T$ and real constants $\kappa,\Lambda$, then
$$S_h+\tau^2-|K|_h^2=2\Lambda+2\kappa T(n,n),\qquad (\operatorname{div}_hK)(Y)-D_Y\tau=\kappa T(n,Y).$$
With $\rho=T(n,n)$ and $j(Y)=-T(n,Y)$, the second equation is $(\operatorname{div}_hK)(Y)-D_Y\tau=-\kappa j(Y)$.

before_manifest_row.title: Worked E0 check: constant-coefficient transport on the three-torus, explicit solution and conserved energy
before_manifest_row.statement:
On $\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$ take $m=1$, $A^0=1$, $A^1=2$, $A^2=A^3=0$, $B=0$,
so the system $(\star)$ of [[def-gr-periodic-symmetric-hyperbolic-system]]
reads $\partial_tu+2\partial_1u=0$, with $u_0\in H^s$ real-valued and $s\ge5$.
This example exhibits the explicit solution on the periodic domain,
$u(t,x)=u_0(x^1-2t,x^2,x^3)$, verifies that it is the E0 solution, and checks
the weighted energy identity $e'(t)=0$ for the energy
$e(t)=\int u(t)^2\,d\mu$ directly.

before_manifest_row.title: Subsidiary system of the dust reduction: Cartan identities, closed homogeneous residual system and vanishing of the residuals
before_manifest_row.statement:
Assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]) and Dependent Choice ([[def-dependent-choice]]), carrying the analytic uniqueness and causal-curve supplier hypotheses.

Let a smooth reduced dust solution have a nondegenerate tentative orthonormal frame for $\gamma$ of signature $(+---)$, a metric-compatible tentative connection, reconstructed algebraic Weyl tensor $C$, prescribed curvature $\overline R$, and dust Schouten tensor $S$ as in [[def-gr-dust-reduction-variables-and-gauge]] and [[def-gr-dust-electric-magnetic-weyl-variables-and-schouten]]. Allow $r\geq0$, with a smooth unit timelike $U$ prescribed also where $r=0$. Assume the parallel-comoving gauge and precisely the reduced equations
$$e_0=U,\quad\Gamma_0{}^i{}_j=0,\quad T^i{}_{0a}=0,\quad\Delta^i{}_{j0a}=0,\quad P_{ab}=Q_{ab}=0,\quad q=U(r)+r\chi=0.$$
Here $a,b=1,2,3$, the first torsion index is the output index, and $P_{ab},Q_{ab}$ are the symmetric tracefree evolution projections of [[lem-gr-dust-reduced-evolution-equations]]. No spatial torsion or spatial curvature residual is assumed zero. Define $F_{jkl}=\nabla^i(C_{ijkl}-\gamma_{i[k}S_{l]j})$, $P_a=F_{0a0}$, and $Q_a=-\epsilon_a{}^{bc}F_{0bc}/2$. Then the spatial components of $(T,\Delta)$ and the vectors $(P,Q)$ satisfy the explicit closed linear homogeneous system constructed in the proof. Its principal part is transport along $U$ for $T,\Delta$ and the curl pair
$$e_0(P_a)+\tfrac12\epsilon_a{}^{bc}e_b(Q_c),\qquad e_0(Q_a)-\tfrac12\epsilon_a{}^{bc}e_b(P_c).$$
It is symmetric hyperbolic on every spacelike initial hypersurface, including one tilted relative to $U$. If all residuals vanish initially, they vanish on its metric domain of determination. Consequently the tentative connection is Levi--Civita, its actual curvature equals $\overline R$, and the resulting metric satisfies the full Einstein-dust equation. The conclusion uses neither division by $r$ nor hypersurface orthogonality of $U$.

before_manifest_row.title: Dust initial data: curvature and connection from (h,K), and the tilted constrained initialization of the Bianchi residuals
before_manifest_row.statement:
Assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]) and Dependent Choice ([[def-dependent-choice]]), carrying the analytic uniqueness and causal-curve supplier hypotheses.

Let $\Sigma$ be a smooth spacelike initial surface with smooth induced Riemannian metric $h$, symmetric second fundamental form $K(X,Y)=g(\nabla_XN,Y)$, rest-mass density $\rho_{\rm mass}\ge0$, fixed $c>0$, and a prescribed smooth future $\gamma$-unit velocity $U_0$, where $\gamma=-g$ has signature $(+---)$. Put $\varepsilon=\rho_{\rm mass}c^2$. Assume the Hamiltonian and momentum constraints of [[thm-gr-constraint-equations-in-normal-frame]] for the initial stress tensor $T_0=\varepsilon U_0^{\flat_g}\otimes U_0^{\flat_g}$, coupling $\kappa>0$ and cosmological constant $\Lambda$. The two lowered factors give the same covariant tensor with $\gamma=-g$. Choose an orientation and oriented tetrads locally for the magnetic contractions. Then locally:

(a) Gauss/Codazzi and the spatial target Ricci equations determine a unique full algebraic curvature tensor. Its full proper Lorentz basis transformation to an oriented tetrad with $e_0=U_0$, followed by the observer electric and magnetic contractions, determines $E_0,B_0$. Boosts may mix these parts.

(b) The tangential metric connection from $(h,K)$, differentiated boost data, and $\omega(U_0)=0$ uniquely determine the entire initial tetrad connection.

(c) At the first jets supplied by the reduced system, every initial torsion, curvature, matter-conservation and Bianchi residual vanishes. In particular the required direction-slot projections are $T^i{}_{0a}=0$ and $\Delta^i{}_{j0a}=0$.

(d) For a future-positive timelike initial conormal $\zeta$, $z=\zeta(U_0)>|w|$ with $w_a=\zeta(e_a)$, the remaining Bianchi components obey $zP+\tfrac12w\times Q=0$, $zQ-\tfrac12w\times P=0$, so vanish. The initial time matrices are positive for every tilt $|v|<1$. Vacuum points remain admitted with prescribed auxiliary velocity.

before_manifest_row.title: Local well-posedness and finite-speed independence of the extension for symmetric hyperbolic systems on a coordinate neighbourhood
before_manifest_row.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $s\ge5$, let $A^\mu,B$ be a periodic symmetric
hyperbolic coefficient family on the open set $O\subseteq\mathbb R^m$, let
$K\subseteq\operatorname{int}K'\subseteq O$ be compact, let $R\ge0$, and let
$T>0$ and $C$ be as in [[thm-gr-periodic-symmetric-hyperbolic-existence]] for
the class $\mathcal S(K,R)$; for every datum $u_0\in\mathcal S(K,R)$ let $u$ be
the solution produced there on $(-T,T)$ with values in $K'$. Then:

**(a) [local existence]** For every $u_0\in\mathcal S(K,R)$ and every
$x_0\in\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$ the solution $u$ is $C^1$ on a neighborhood of
$(0,x_0)$ in $(-T,T)\times\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$ and solves $(\star)$ pointwise
there.

**(b) [finite speed / independence of the extension]** Let $\lambda_0>0$ be
determined by the coefficient bounds on a compact set containing the values of
the solutions in the following sense: for a truncated cone
$$D:=\{(t,x):0\le t\le t_0,\ d(x,x_0)\le\lambda(t_0-t)\}$$
with $t_0<T$, $\lambda\ge\lambda_0$, lying in a single chart of $\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$
in which the coordinate representation of $A^\mu$ satisfies
$\lambda\,A^0+\xi_iA^i\ge0$ for all unit $\xi$ (which holds for $\lambda$ large
enough by clause (a) of [[lem-gr-finite-speed-independence-of-extension]]),
let $u,v$ be solutions of two periodic symmetric hyperbolic systems whose
coefficient functions agree on a neighborhood of $D$ in the independent variables and on one common open state set containing both solution ranges, with
$u(0,\cdot)=v(0,\cdot)$ on the ball $\{d(x,x_0)\le\lambda t_0\}$. Then
$u=v$ on $D$.

**(c) [local uniqueness and stability]** If two classical solutions of the same
system on a common interval have values in $K$, $H^s$ norms at most $R$ and the
same initial value, they coincide; and the continuous-dependence estimate of
[[thm-gr-periodic-symmetric-hyperbolic-uniqueness-stability]] clause (b) holds
for the solutions of clause (a).

before_manifest_row.title: Propagation of the harmonic gauge and of the Einstein constraints: a constrained reduced solution is an Einstein solution
before_manifest_row.statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be a smooth time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold, let
$\Sigma\subseteq M$ be a smooth spacelike hypersurface
([[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]]) with future unit normal
field $\mathfrak n$ and tangential frame $(e_i)$
([[lem-gr-spacelike-hypersurface-normal-and-second-fundamental-form]]), and let
$U$ be an open neighborhood of $\Sigma$ carrying a smooth background metric
$\bar g$ and a smooth symmetric tensor $T$ with $\nabla^aT_{ab}=0$ on $U$. Let
$H$ and $E$ be the gauge vector and Einstein residual of
[[def-gr-harmonic-gauge-and-reduced-equations]]. Suppose:

1. $(g,T)$ solves the reduced Einstein equation on $U$;
2. $H=0$ on $\Sigma$;
3. the constraint residuals vanish on $\Sigma$: $E(\mathfrak n,\mathfrak n)=0$
   and $E(\mathfrak n,e_i)=0$ for all $i$.

Then there is an open neighborhood $W\subseteq U$ of $\Sigma$ on which $H=0$ and
$E=0$; consequently $G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}=\kappa T_{ab}$ on $W$, so $g$ solves
the Einstein equation with the prescribed matter tensor there.

before_manifest_row.title: Local existence for the reduced Einstein equation from Cauchy data on a spacelike slice
before_manifest_row.statement:
Let $M$ be a smooth four-manifold carrying a chart $(x^0=t,x^1,x^2,x^3)$ whose
domain $U$ contains the slice $\Sigma:=\{t=0\}$, let $\bar g$ be a smooth
background metric on $U$ with its Levi--Civita connection $\bar\nabla$, and let
$T$ be a smooth symmetric covariant $2$-tensor on $U$ together with the
background-covariant derivatives needed below (the matter field data). Suppose
smooth functions $g^0_{ab},g^1_{ab}$ on $\Sigma\cap U$ are given such that:

1. $g^0_{ab}$ are the components of a smooth Lorentzian metric on
   $\Sigma\cap U$ with $g^{00}_0<0$ and positive definite spatial block
   $(g_0^{ij})$;
2. $g^1_{ab}$ is symmetric and agrees on $\Sigma$ with the components of
   $\bar\nabla_0g_{ab}$ for some smooth extension $g$ of $g^0$ to $U$;
3. the harmonic-gauge condition $H^a=0$ holds on $\Sigma\cap U$ for the pair
   $(g,\bar g)$ ([[def-gr-harmonic-gauge-and-reduced-equations]]).

Then there is an open neighborhood $V\subseteq U$ of $\Sigma\cap U$ and a smooth
metric $g$ on $V$ with $g|_{\Sigma\cap U}=g^0$ and
$\bar\nabla_0g_{ab}|_{\Sigma\cap U}=g^1_{ab}$, solving the **reduced Einstein
equation** with the given background $\bar g$ and matter tensor $T$
([[def-gr-harmonic-gauge-and-reduced-equations]]) on $V$.

before_manifest_row.title: Model configurations, interface readouts, operational models, data records and the analysis vocabulary of the experiment interface
before_manifest_row.statement:
## Definition

Adopt the unit conventions of [[def-gr-si-unit-and-coordinate-conventions]], the
spacetime postulate of [[post-gr-spacetime-and-classical-domain]] and the
clock, free-fall and light-ray postulates of
[[post-gr-ideal-clocks-and-free-fall]]. This definition fixes the vocabulary in
which the framework's empirical layer is stated: it names model
configurations, the readouts assigned to them, operational models, data
records, calibration declarations and declared uncertainty bounds. It selects
no experiment, records no value and asserts no comparison.

**(a) Model configurations.** Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth
Lorentzian four-manifold with metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]], [[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]). A **model
configuration** is a finite tuple $D=(d_1,\dots,d_r)$ whose entries are objects
of the following kinds, each carrying the domain, parametrization and
regularity required by the cited item:

- a *worldline entry*: a $C^1$ future timelike worldline $h:I\to M$ on an
  interval $I$ with nonempty interior, parametrized by proper time, so that its
  four-velocity $U:=h'$ satisfies $g(U,U)=-c^2$
  ([[def-gr-timelike-worldline-and-proper-time]],
  [[lem-gr-proper-time-reparametrization-and-four-velocity]]), or the
  restriction of such a worldline to a subinterval;
- an *observer entry*: an observer at a point, that is a future unit timelike
  vector $n$ with $g(n,n)=-1$, or a smooth observer congruence
  ([[def-gr-observer-and-rest-space]],
  [[def-gr-observer-congruence-and-adapted-charts]]);
- a *ray entry*: a $C^1$ future-directed null geodesic $\eta:J\to M$ of
  $\nabla$, so that $\nabla_{\eta'}\eta'=0$, $g(\eta',\eta')=0$ and
  $\eta'$ is future-directed ([[def-geodesic-of-an-affine-connection]],
  [[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]],
  [[post-gr-ideal-clocks-and-free-fall]] clause (iii));
- a *chart entry*: a smooth chart $(U,x)$ of $M$ ([[def-smooth-manifold]]);
- a *detector entry*: the data of the ideal two-body detector of the
  linearized-wave regime, namely a TT linearized-wave datum, a reference point
  $x_0$, a separation vector $\delta\ne0$ with $\delta^0=0$, the arm direction
  $e_\delta$, and a parameter value $s$, as in
  [[def-gr-linearized-wave-regime-and-detector-coupling]] clauses (a)-(c);
- a *parameter entry*: a finite tuple of real numbers in a declared subset of
  $\mathbb R^m$, each component with declared units;
- an *annotation entry*: a finite string recording declared conditions of the
  configuration and, where a datum is taken from a report, the bibliographic
  identification of that report.

A model configuration is a description of a hypothetical model situation. The
tuple asserts nothing about any apparatus and nothing about nature, and no
clause of this definition asserts that a configuration with prescribed entries
exists: existence claims belong to the items that construct the entries.

**(b) Readouts.** Let $D$ be a model configuration. The following **readouts**
are defined whenever $D$ contains the entries named in the clause together with
the stated incidence conditions; each is a real number or a finite tuple of
real numbers determined by the entries of $D$.

1. *Frequency ratio and redshift.* Suppose $D$ contains a ray entry
   $\eta:J\to M$ with tangent $W:=\eta'$, worldline entries $h_E:I_E\to M$ and
   $h_R:I_R\to M$ with four-velocities $U_E,U_R$, and parameter values
   $s_E<s_R$ in $J$, $t_E\in I_E$, $t_R\in I_R$ with $\eta(s_E)=h_E(t_E)$ and
   $\eta(s_R)=h_R(t_R)$. The **observer energies** of the ray at the two events
   relative to the unit observers $U_E/c$ and $U_R/c$ are

   $$E_E:=-c\,g_{\eta(s_E)}\bigl(W(s_E),U_E(t_E)/c\bigr),\qquad E_R:=-c\,g_{\eta(s_R)}\bigl(W(s_R),U_R(t_R)/c\bigr),$$

   the values of clause (a) of
   [[def-gr-observer-relative-energy-and-momentum]] for those observers; both
   are strictly positive by claim 1 of
   [[lem-gr-observer-pairing-with-future-causal-vectors]], because $W$ is
   nonzero future null and $U_E/c$, $U_R/c$ are future unit timelike. The
   **frequency-ratio readout** and the **redshift readout** are

   $$\mathcal F:=\frac{E_R}{E_E}=\frac{g_{\eta(s_R)}\bigl(W(s_R),U_R(t_R)\bigr)}{g_{\eta(s_E)}\bigl(W(s_E),U_E(t_E)\bigr)},\qquad z:=\frac{E_E}{E_R}-1=\frac1{\mathcal F}-1 .$$

2. *Radar round-trip proper time.* Suppose $D$ contains worldline entries
   $h_R:I_R\to M$ (the receiver) and $h_C:I_C\to M$ (the reflector), parameter
   values $t_1<t_2$ in $I_R$ and $s_C\in I_C$, and ray entries $\eta_1,\eta_2$
   whose parameter intervals contain values exhibiting
   $\eta_1(s_1)=h_R(t_1)$, $\eta_1(s_1')=h_C(s_C)$ with $s_1<s_1'$, and
   $\eta_2(s_2)=h_C(s_C)$, $\eta_2(s_2')=h_R(t_2)$ with $s_2<s_2'$. The
   **radar readout** is the receiver proper-time increment
   $\Delta\tau:=t_2-t_1$ between emission and reception. It is independent of
   the affine parametrizations of $\eta_1,\eta_2$, which enter only through the
   incidence statements ([[def-gr-timelike-worldline-and-proper-time]] clause
   (d), [[lem-gr-proper-time-reparametrization-and-four-velocity]]).

3. *Deflection angle.* Suppose $D$ contains a ray entry $\eta:J\to M$ with
   tangent $W$, parameter values $s_1<s_2$ in $J$, observer entries $n_1,n_2$ at
   $p_1:=\eta(s_1)$ and $p_2:=\eta(s_2)$, and an isometric identification
   $\Phi:T_{p_1}M\to T_{p_2}M$, by which is meant a linear isomorphism with
   $g_{p_2}(\Phi v,\Phi w)=g_{p_1}(v,w)$ for all $v,w\in T_{p_1}M$ and
   $\Phi(n_1)=n_2$. Put $q_i:=h_{n_i}(W(s_i))$, the spatial projection of
   clause (b) of [[def-gr-observer-and-rest-space]], and suppose $q_1,q_2\ne0$.
   Then $|q_i|_{n_i}:=\sqrt{g_{p_i}(q_i,q_i)}>0$, because $g_{p_i}$ is positive
   definite on the rest space ([[lem-gr-observer-projection-decomposition]]),
   and $\Phi(q_1)$ lies in $n_2^{\perp}$ with
   $g_{p_2}(\Phi q_1,\Phi q_1)=g_{p_1}(q_1,q_1)$. The **deflection cosine**
   and **deflection readout** are

   $$\kappa:=\frac{g_{p_2}\bigl(\Phi(q_1),q_2\bigr)}{|q_1|_{n_1}\,|q_2|_{n_2}}\in[-1,1],\qquad \Theta:=\arccos\kappa,$$

   where the bound is the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality in the real inner product
   space $(n_2^{\perp},g_{p_2})$
   ([[def-inner-product-space]],
   [[thm-cauchy-schwarz-for-real-and-complex-inner-product-spaces]]) and
   $\arccos$ is the principal inverse cosine of
   [[def-principal-inverse-sine-and-cosine]].

4. *Azimuthal increment and perihelion advance.* Suppose $D$ contains a
   worldline entry $h:I\to M$, a chart entry $(U,x)$ and an annotation entry
   designating the coordinate $x^2$ as the azimuth and declaring two parameter
   values $t_1<t_2$ in $I$ with $h(t_1),h(t_2)\in U$ to be successive passages
   of the worldline through the minimum of the coordinate $x^1$ within $U$. Then
   the **azimuthal-increment readout** and the **perihelion-advance readout**
   are

   $$\Delta\varphi:=x^2\bigl(h(t_2)\bigr)-x^2\bigl(h(t_1)\bigr),\qquad A:=\Delta\varphi-2\pi .$$

   The designation of the two passages is a declared condition carried by the
   annotation, not a consequence of the other entries, and the readout is a
   chart datum: it is not asserted to be invariant under changes of chart.

5. *Arrival times.* Suppose $D$ contains worldline entries $h_E,h_R$, a finite
   family of ray entries $\eta_1,\dots,\eta_N$ and parameter values such that
   $\eta_k$ joins an event of $h_E$ to $h_R(t_k)$, with $t_1<\cdots<t_N$ in
   $I_R$. The **arrival-time readout** is the tuple $(t_1,\dots,t_N)$ of
   receiver proper-time values.

6. *Strain.* Suppose $D$ contains a detector entry of (a) and a parameter
   value at which the quantity under the square root of clause (c) of
   [[def-gr-linearized-wave-regime-and-detector-coupling]] is positive. The
   **strain readout** is the value $S_\delta(s)$ of the strain function of that
   clause.

**(c) Operational models.** An **operational model** is a tuple
$M=(S,\Theta,\theta,D,F)$ in which $S$ is a nonempty set, the *preparation
index set*; $\Theta\subseteq\mathbb R^m$ is a nonempty *parameter set* whose
coordinates carry declared units; $\theta:S\to\Theta$ is a surjection, the
*parameter map*; $D$ assigns to each $s\in S$ a model configuration $D(s)$ of
(a); and for some integer $d\ge1$ a map $F:\Theta\to\mathbb R^d$ is a
**prediction map** for $D$, subject to the declared interpretation $(*)$: for
every $s\in S$, each component of $F(\theta(s))$ is a value that the
framework's definitions, postulates and proved consequences assign to a
readout of (b) of the configuration $D(s)$, with every intermediate quantity,
event, frame, sign and unit declared. In particular, a component asserted to be
a frequency ratio, redshift, radar, deflection, azimuthal, advance,
arrival-time or strain value must be the corresponding readout of (b) for
entries that the configuration contains, and a component read from a cited
prediction theorem must be a value that theorem assigns to entries of $D(s)$
satisfying its hypotheses. Condition $(*)$ is a declared interpretation that
reviewers check when the model is used; it is not a consequence of the tuple
structure, and no clause of this definition asserts that any apparatus realizes
$M$ or that any component of $F$ is measured.

**(d) Data records.** A **data record** is a tuple $R=(N,z,\varepsilon,a)$ with
an integer $N\ge1$; $z=(z_1,\dots,z_N)$ with $z_k\in\mathbb R^d$;
$\varepsilon=(\varepsilon_1,\dots,\varepsilon_N)$ with
$\varepsilon_k\in[0,\infty)^d$; and $a=(a_1,\dots,a_N)$ a finite tuple of
*condition annotations* as in (a). The record declares: for each $k$, the value
of the readout under the condition annotated by $a_k$ lies in the closed box
$\prod_{j=1}^d[z_{k,j}-\varepsilon_{k,j},\,z_{k,j}+\varepsilon_{k,j}]$, in the
declared units. A data record contains no probability space, random variable,
distribution, sampling law, independence assumption, likelihood or coverage
statement; it declares nothing about how the values $z_k$ were produced and
nothing about the correctness of any calibration.

**(e) Calibration declarations.** Let $Z$ be a nonempty set of declared
*instrument-output values*. A **calibration declaration** is a tuple
$C=(Z,c,\delta,h)$ with $c:Z\to\mathbb R^d$, $\delta:Z\to[0,\infty)^d$ and $h$
a condition annotation as in (a); it declares that for every $z\in Z$ obtained
under the condition annotated by $h$, the value of the declared readout lies in
the closed box
$\prod_{j=1}^d[c_j(z)-\delta_j(z),\,c_j(z)+\delta_j(z)]$ in the declared units.
A **calibration record** is a data record of (d) whose declared readout is the
value of the calibration map's output. The declaration asserts no accuracy
beyond the bound $\delta$ and no statistical property of $c$ or $\delta$.

**(f) Uncertainty vocabulary.** For a data record of (d), the **declared
uncertainty** of the $k$-th datum is the vector $\varepsilon_k$; a **source
label** is an element of the finite declared set
$\{\text{calibration},\ \text{systematic},\ \text{sampling-variability},\
\text{rounding},\ \text{other}\}$ attached to a bound; and a **total declared
bound** for a value computed from finitely many recorded values by a declared
finite arithmetic expression is any $B\in[0,\infty)$ for which the declaration
states: whenever each recorded value lies in its declared closed box, the
computed value lies in $[\hat y-B,\hat y+B]$ for the declared number $\hat y$
(for instance, for a sum of recorded scalars the sum of the recorded bounds is
such a bound). Every uncertainty entry is a declared constraint of the form in
(d) and (e); no probability law, coverage probability, confidence level,
p-value or posterior is defined by this vocabulary.

**(g) Comparison claims are separate.** A claim that a data record $R$ and an
operational model $M$ are consistent, or that $R$ supports, refutes or fails to
distinguish $M$, is not part of (a)-(f): it requires its own statement, an
explicitly declared comparison rule, and adequate primary-report and analysis
prerequisites. A declared rule of the form "$t\in\Theta$ is consistent with the
one-point hard-bound record $R$ exactly when $F(t)$ lies in the record's closed
box", together with the resulting consistency set
$C(R,M):=\{t\in\Theta:F(t)\in\prod_{j}[z_{1,j}-\varepsilon_{1,j},\,z_{1,j}+\varepsilon_{1,j}]\}$,
is a comparison rule in this sense; it is conditional on the record's declared
bounds and on the interpretation $(*)$, and it establishes neither the truth of
a postulate nor the correctness of any apparatus. The source design's research
prerequisite labelled M20, the primary-report and analysis layer, is not
supplied by the items of this page: no reported measurement and no experiment
item occurs here. The framework's model-side prediction content for the
readouts of (b) currently consists of the restricted redshift theorems
`pthm-gr-schwarzschild-stationary-redshift` (static observers in the
Schwarzschild exterior model) and `pthm-gr-flrw-cosmological-redshift`
(comoving observers in a homogeneous cosmological model) for readout 1, and of
the ideal-detector definition `def-gr-linearized-wave-regime-and-detector-coupling`
with the response theorem `pthm-gr-plane-wave-tidal-detector-response` for
readout 6; the propagation-delay, deflection, perihelion-advance and
arrival-time readouts of 2-5 have no in-framework prediction theorem yet and
are recorded as report destinations in
`rem-gr-primary-report-research-queue`. These item names are nonlogical
status pointers; they add no premise to this definition.

**(h) Well-definedness and scope.** All components of (a)-(g) are finite tuples
of sets, maps, curves and real numbers with declared domains and units. The
constructions use no choice principle beyond those already assumed by the cited
suppliers: [[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]] uses countable choice
([[def-countable-choice]]) for the canonical smooth structures of tangent
bundles, and nothing here uses any further choice. No measurability,
integrability, completeness, differentiability or convergence beyond the cited
items is used. Clause (c) evaluates a prediction only at parameter values for
which the cited items supply its ingredients, and each readout of (b) is
defined only for configurations carrying the stated entries and incidence
conditions, so this definition asserts no existence of worldlines, rays,
charts, detectors or configurations. The vocabulary asserts no measurement, no
apparatus behaviour, no empirical support or refutation, no value of the
constant $c$ or of any other physical parameter, and no statistical inference.

before_manifest_row.title: Worked instance of the interface vocabulary on the cosmological redshift slot: an explicit de Sitter ray family, an operational model and the exact window of an illustrative bounded record
before_manifest_row.statement:
## Example

Fix real constants $c>0$, $A>0$, $H>0$, $t_0\in\mathbb R$, $r_0\in\mathbb R$ and
adopt the homogeneous cosmological model of
[[post-gr-flrw-homogeneous-cosmological-model]] in its vacuum sector, with the
FLRW model datum $(I,\Sigma,\gamma,k,a)$ given by $I=\mathbb R$, the standard
Euclidean $\mathbb R^3$ in its standard coordinates, $k=0$ and
$a(t):=A\exp\bigl(H(t-t_0)\bigr)$ ([[def-gr-flrw-model-data]]). Let $g$ be the
metric, $\nabla$ its metric-selected connection, $n=c^{-1}\partial_t$ the
comoving congruence and $\gamma_x(t):=(t,x)$ the comoving worldline through
$x\in\mathbb R^3$ ([[lem-gr-flrw-metric-and-comoving-data]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]]). The point of the example is the
interface arithmetic of
[[def-gr-observation-and-analysis-architecture]], not the datum.

**(a) An explicit ray family.** For $s\in(0,\infty)$ define

$$\eta(s):=\Bigl(t_0+\frac1H\log(Hs),\ \Bigl(r_0+\frac{c}{AH^2s},\,0,\,0\Bigr)\Bigr).$$

Then $\eta$ is a smooth curve in $M=\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^3$; its tangent
$W=\eta'$ has components

$$W^t(s)=\frac{1}{Hs}>0,\qquad W^1(s)=-\frac{c}{AH^2s^2},\qquad W^2(s)=W^3(s)=0,$$

and $W$ is future-directed and null; moreover $\eta$ is a geodesic with affine
parameter $s$, and along it

$$a\bigl(t(s)\bigr)=AHs .$$

By clause (iii) of [[post-gr-ideal-clocks-and-free-fall]] the model assigns
$\eta$ to an ideal light ray.

**(b) The operational model.** Let $s_R>0$ and put $t_R:=t(s_R)$,
$p_R:=\eta(s_R)$, $a_R:=a(t_R)=AHs_R$. For each $a_E\in(0,a_R)$ put
$s_E:=a_E/(AH)$, $t_E:=t(s_E)$ and $p_E:=\eta(s_E)$. Define
$S:=\Theta:=(0,a_R)$, $\theta:=\mathrm{id}$, and let $D(a_E)$ be the model
configuration of clause (a) of [[def-gr-observation-and-analysis-architecture]]
whose entries are: the comoving congruence $n$; the comoving receiver worldline
through $p_R$ and the comoving emitter worldline through $p_E$, each
parametrized by cosmic time; the ray $\eta$ with the parameter values
$s_E<s_R$ and the events $p_E=\eta(s_E)$, $p_R=\eta(s_R)$; and the annotation
declaring that the readout to be computed is the redshift readout of clause
(b)1; the ambient datum, metric and connection are those of the Example. Let
$F:\Theta\to(0,\infty)$ be that redshift readout itself, $F(a_E):=z(a_E)$. Then
$M_{\mathrm{op}}:=(S,\Theta,\theta,D,F)$ is an operational model for the
redshift readout $z$ in the sense of clause (c) of
[[def-gr-observation-and-analysis-architecture]] with the prediction

$$F(a_E)=\frac{a_R}{a_E}-1=\frac{s_R}{s_E}-1,$$

and $F$ is a strictly decreasing bijection of $(0,a_R)$ onto $(0,\infty)$.

**(c) An illustrative record and its exact window.** Declare the one-point data
record $R$ of clause (d) of [[def-gr-observation-and-analysis-architecture]]
with $N=1$, $d=1$, $z_1=5/8$ and $\varepsilon_1=1/8$, and with condition
annotation "cosmological redshift readout of the de Sitter configuration with
fixed $a_R$", so that the record's declared closed box is
$[z_1-\varepsilon_1,z_1+\varepsilon_1]=[1/2,3/4]$;
these are *declared illustrative values*, not a measurement, and the condition
annotation identifies them as such. Declare the comparison rule of clause (g)
of [[def-gr-observation-and-analysis-architecture]] that a parameter
$a_E\in\Theta$ is *consistent* with $R$ exactly when $z(a_E)=F(a_E)$ lies in
the record's closed box $[1/2,3/4]$, equivalently when
$1+z(a_E)=a_R/a_E\in[3/2,7/4]$. Then the consistency set is

$$C(R,M_{\mathrm{op}})=\Bigl[\frac{a_R}{7/4},\ \frac{a_R}{3/2}\Bigr]=\Bigl[\frac47a_R,\ \frac23a_R\Bigr],$$

a nonempty closed interval of exact length $\frac{2}{21}a_R$; its endpoints
satisfy $F(4a_R/7)=7/4-1=3/4$ and $F(2a_R/3)=3/2-1=1/2$, and both lie strictly
inside $(0,a_R)$. For the declared illustrative normalisation $a_R=1$ in the
length unit of the datum the window is $[4/7,2/3]$ with length $2/21$ in that
unit.

**(d) Scope.** Every number in (c) is a declared illustrative value supplied to
instantiate the vocabulary; the example asserts no apparatus, no calibration
correctness, no measurement, no sampling model, no statistical inference and no
empirical support or refutation of the cosmological redshift theorem or of any
postulate. The model of (b) is hypothetical: no claim is made that $H$ and the
vacuum sector satisfy the field law for any particular cosmological parameter,
and no observation or reported dataset enters.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The constants $c>0$, $A>0$, $H>0$, $t_0,r_0\in\mathbb R$; the FLRW datum of the Example with $I=\mathbb R$, the standard Euclidean $\mathbb R^3$, $k=0$ and $a(t)=A\exp(H(t-t_0))$; its metric $g=-c^2dt^2+a(t)^2\gamma$ in the product chart $(t,x^1,x^2,x^3)$, its metric-selected connection $\nabla$ and comoving congruence $n=c^{-1}\partial_t$; the curve $\eta$ of (a) with tangent $W$; the declared constants $s_R>0$, $a_R=AHs_R$ and, for each $a_E\in(0,a_R)$, the values $s_E=a_E/(AH)$ and events $p_E,p_R$; and the declared illustrative record $R$ and comparison rule of (c).

[A1] Adopted model: the spacetime geometry of the homogeneous cosmological model is an FLRW model datum with metric $g=-c^2dt^2+a(t)^2\gamma$ and comoving congruence $n=c^{-1}\partial_t$, and in the vacuum sector no matter is present ([[post-gr-flrw-homogeneous-cosmological-model]] clauses (i) and (ii)). The ideal light-ray rule is clause (iii) of [[post-gr-ideal-clocks-and-free-fall]]: ideal light rays are future null geodesics.

[L1] In the product chart the Christoffel symbols of $\nabla$ are $\Gamma^0{}_{ij}=(a\dot a/c^2)\gamma_{ij}$, $\Gamma^i{}_{0j}=(\dot a/a)\delta^i{}_j$ and $\Gamma^i{}_{jk}={}^{(3)}\Gamma^i{}_{jk}$, all others zero; on the standard Euclidean $\mathbb R^3$ one has ${}^{(3)}\Gamma^i{}_{jk}=0$, so with $\dot a=Ha$ the only nonzero symbols are $\Gamma^0{}_{11}=Ha^2/c^2$ and $\Gamma^i{}_{0j}=H\delta^i{}_j$ ([[lem-gr-flrw-christoffel-symbols]], [[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]]).

[L2] A smooth curve is a geodesic with affine parameter $s$ exactly when, in a chart, $\dot V^a+\sum_{b,c}\Gamma^a{}_{bc}V^bV^c=0$ for $a=0,1,2,3$ on every parameter subinterval lying in the chart, where $V$ is the tangent ([[def-geodesic-of-an-affine-connection]], [[prop-coordinate-geodesic-equation]]).

[L3] The metric components in the product chart are $g_{00}=-c^2$, $g_{0i}=0$, $g_{ij}=a(t)^2\gamma_{ij}$; a nonzero vector is future-directed exactly when $g(V,\partial_t)<0$, and null exactly when $g(V,V)=0$; the comoving curve $\gamma_x(t)=(t,x)$ is a future timelike worldline with four-velocity $U=\partial_t=cn$, $g(U,U)=-c^2$, and its parameter $t$ is its proper time up to an additive constant ([[lem-gr-flrw-metric-and-comoving-data]] clauses (a)-(b), [[def-gr-timelike-worldline-and-proper-time]], [[lem-gr-proper-time-reparametrization-and-four-velocity]], [[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]], [[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]).

[L4] The exponential is smooth on $\mathbb R$ with $\exp'=\exp$, the natural logarithm is smooth and strictly increasing on $(0,\infty)$ with $\log'(\xi)=1/\xi$ and $\exp(\log \xi)=\xi$, and the chain and product rules apply ([[def-real-exponential-function-and-e]], [[thm-derivative-of-exponential]], [[def-natural-logarithm]], [[thm-logarithm-derivative-and-integral]], [[def-derivative]], [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]], [[thm-chain-rule]]).

[L5] Redshift theorem: for the adopted model with an FLRW datum and a future null geodesic $\eta:J\to M$ on which the observer energies $E(s)=-c\,g_{\eta(s)}(V(s),n(\eta(s)))$, $V=\eta'$, $n=c^{-1}\partial_t$, satisfy $E(s)>0$, and for $s_E<s_R$, one has $E(s_R)/E(s_E)=a(t_E)/a(t_R)$ and, with $1+z:=E(s_E)/E(s_R)$, $1+z=a(t_R)/a(t_E)$ ([[pthm-gr-flrw-cosmological-redshift]] clauses (b)-(c)).

[L6] Interface vocabulary: a readout is defined for a model configuration carrying the required entries; an operational model is a tuple $(S,\Theta,\theta,D,F)$ with $F$ subject to the interpretation $(*)$; a data record declares that the readout lies in the closed box $\prod_j[z_{1,j}-\varepsilon_{1,j},z_{1,j}+\varepsilon_{1,j}]$ and contains no probability space, sampling law or coverage statement; and a comparison claim requires a separately declared rule ([[def-gr-observation-and-analysis-architecture]] clauses (b)1, (c), (d), (g)).

[L7] The observer energy of clause (a) of [[def-gr-observer-relative-energy-and-momentum]] for the unit observer $U/c$ is $E=-c\,g(W,U/c)=-g(W,U)$; for the comoving worldlines $U=\partial_t$ this is $-g(W,\partial_t)$.

before_manifest_row.statement:
## Statement

Scope-and-queue record for the empirical layer of the classical gravitational
framework, stated in the vocabulary of
[[def-gr-observation-and-analysis-architecture]].

(i) **Status of the empirical layer.** The source design of the experimental
interface reserves a definition of the observation and analysis architecture
(delivered by [[def-gr-observation-and-analysis-architecture]]) and this
primary-report research queue. No experiment item is authored in this batch and
no measured value is recorded anywhere in it. The research label M20 of the
source design, the primary-report and analysis layer, remains unsupplied:
before any experiment item can be authored on a destination, the actual primary
report must be retrieved and read in full, and the record must carry the
apparatus and preparation, the operational definitions of the measured
quantities, the calibration model, the sampling and error model, the treatment
of systematic effects, the measured values with their reported uncertainties,
and the source's own limitations. Secondary surveys and lecture notes describe
these report families and their analysis structure; they are not substitutes
for the primary reports and no number attributed to any of them is asserted
here.

(ii) **Report families.** The source design names six *primary-report search
destinations*, that is, families of published reports to retrieve and read in
full; no destination is evidence for any postulate. For each family the
in-framework model-side content that a comparison would consume is named by its
item, and the missing predictions are recorded as future obligations rather
than assumed.

1. *Redshift and clock comparisons.* Comparisons of identical frequency
   standards or clocks at rest at different locations in a gravitational field,
   including transported-clock comparisons (Will section 2.1.3; Carroll
   (7.61)-(7.62); Tong section 1.2.5). Model-side content available: the
   frequency-ratio and redshift readouts of
   [[def-gr-observation-and-analysis-architecture]] clause (b), realized for
   static observers by `pthm-gr-schwarzschild-stationary-redshift` and for
   comoving observers by `pthm-gr-flrw-cosmological-redshift`. What is still
   missing for a comparison: the apparatus, calibration, line-shape and
   statistical analysis of an actual report, as in (i).

2. *Light-propagation delay.* Measurements of the variation of round-trip
   travel times of signals passing near a massive body, analysed differentially
   against an ephemeris (Will section 4.1.2; Carroll printed p. 181). The
   interface readout is the radar readout of clause (b)2 of
   [[def-gr-observation-and-analysis-architecture]]. Model-side content: no
   in-framework prediction theorem for the round-trip delay exists in the
   library; a restricted prediction for a specified ray family and reflector
   worldline would have to be authored before any comparison.

3. *Light deflection.* Measurements of the change in angular separation of
   sources whose lines of sight pass near a massive body, by optical astrometry
   or radio interferometry, with a fitted deflection coefficient (Will section
   4.1.1; Carroll printed p. 181). The interface readout is the deflection
   readout of clause (b)3. Model-side content: no in-framework prediction
   theorem for the deflection angle of a specified ray exists; it is a future
   obligation.

4. *Perihelion advance.* Measurements of the residual precession of an
   almost-elliptical planetary orbit after the perturbations of the other
   bodies and the precession of the equinoxes have been modelled and removed,
   analysed over long astrometric baselines (Will section 4.2; Carroll
   (7.56)-(7.57)). The interface readout is the perihelion-advance readout of
   clause (b)4. Model-side content: the restricted Schwarzschild page supplies
   circular-orbit and photon-sphere predictions only
   (`pthm-gr-schwarzschild-circular-orbit-predictions`); a prediction of the
   advance of an eccentric orbit is a future obligation.

5. *Binary-system timing.* Analyses of pulse arrival-time series of
   relativistic binary pulsars, in which orbital and relativistic parameters
   are fitted to a timing model (Will section 6.1). The interface readout is
   the arrival-time readout of clause (b)5. Model-side content: the framework
   contains no binary dynamics, no gravitational-wave source model and no
   timing-model theorem; these are future obligations in a different module.

6. *Interferometric strain.* Measurements of strain by laser-interferometric
   observatories and proposals for pulsar timing arrays (Will section 7.1;
   Carroll Ch. 6; Tong sections 5.2-5.3). The interface readout is the strain
   readout of clause (b)6. Model-side content: the ideal two-body detector of
   `def-gr-linearized-wave-regime-and-detector-coupling` clause (c) and the
   response theorem `pthm-gr-plane-wave-tidal-detector-response`. What is still
   missing: a source model producing the waveform, the propagation of light in
   the instrument, readout and noise models, calibration, and a statistical
   analysis; without them no comparison is instantiable.

(iii) **Analysis obligations for every future comparison.** Each comparison
will require a declared comparison rule of clause (g) of
[[def-gr-observation-and-analysis-architecture]], an operational model whose
prediction map satisfies condition $(*)$, a data record with declared closed
bounds or separately defined source-reported estimates and scales, a declared
treatment of calibration and of the dominant systematic effects, and, for
reported data, the primary report's own sampling and error model. Agreement of
a prediction with a record tests the combined model, apparatus and analysis
assumptions; it is evidence, not a deductive proof of the model or of any
postulate.

(iv) **Qualifications any future comparison must carry.** The following are
part of the interface contract and must appear in any consuming item: (a) model
predictions are conditional on the adopted postulates and on the explicit
hypotheses of the prediction theorem; (b) observations are reported under the
source's conditions and limitations; (c) finite-sample agreement does not
establish a postulate or a model, and a finite hard-bound record does not by
itself determine a unique parameter; (d) a p-value would not be the probability
that a theory is false and a confidence level would not be a posterior
probability; (e) reported standard uncertainties are not hard bounds and carry
no coverage guarantee; (f) every conclusion inherits the calibration
dependence, systematic limitations and selection assumptions of the source.

(v) **Pointer.** The primary observations, when they are eventually recorded,
belong in experiment items with their own empirical contracts; the comparison
arithmetic belongs in a separate proved item. This remark is a queue and status
pointer only: it supplies no independent empirical conclusion and no certainty.

before_manifest_row.title: Counterexample: a bounded one-point record of the cosmological redshift slot does not determine the emitter scale factor
before_manifest_row.statement:
## Statement refuted

In the operational model $M_{\mathrm{op}}$ of
[[ex-gr-cosmological-redshift-interface-record-window]] clause (b), with the
declared comparison rule of clause (c) of that example and its declared
one-point record with positive declared uncertainty, the parameter is
determined uniquely: if two parameters $a_E,a_E'\in(0,a_R)$ of
$M_{\mathrm{op}}$ are consistent with the record, then $a_E=a_E'$.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The de Sitter FLRW configuration, the operational model
$M_{\mathrm{op}}=(S,\Theta,\theta,D,F)$ with $S=\Theta=(0,a_R)$,
$\theta=\mathrm{id}$ and redshift readout $F(a_E)=a_R/a_E-1$, the declared
one-point record $R$ with closed box $[1/2,3/4]$ on $z$, and the declared
comparison rule that $a_E$ is consistent with $R$ exactly when
$F(a_E)=z(a_E)\in[1/2,3/4]$. All of these are declared illustrative structures
of the worked instance; none is a measurement.

[F1] The worked instance: the operational model of
[[ex-gr-cosmological-redshift-interface-record-window]] clause (b) has
parameter set $(0,a_R)$ and prediction map $F(a_E)=a_R/a_E-1=z(a_E)$; its
declared record has $N=1$, $d=1$, $z_1=5/8$, $\varepsilon_1=1/8$, so that the
declared closed box is $[1/2,3/4]$; its declared comparison rule makes $a_E$
consistent exactly when $F(a_E)=z(a_E)$ lies in that box; and it records the
consistency set $C(R,M_{\mathrm{op}})=[4a_R/7,2a_R/3]$ in clauses (b)-(c).

[L1] Reciprocal ratio windows: for $a_*>0$ and $0<u_1\le u_2$ the preimage
under $a\mapsto a_*/a$ of $[u_1,u_2]$ is $[a_*/u_2,a_*/u_1]$, and that map is
strictly decreasing and injective ([[lem-gr-reciprocal-ratio-window]] claims
2-4).

## Counterexample

**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 (Two consistent parameters.) Let $a_1:=4a_R/7$ and $a_2:=2a_R/3$, both defined since $a_R>0$. They lie in the parameter set $(0,a_R)$ because $0<4/7<2/3<1$. Their predictions are $F(a_1)=a_R/(4a_R/7)-1=7/4-1=3/4$ and $F(a_2)=a_R/(2a_R/3)-1=3/2-1=1/2$ by field arithmetic; both values lie in the declared closed box $[1/2,3/4]$. Hence $a_1$ and $a_2$ are both consistent with the record under the declared comparison rule. [F1, L1, algebra]

1.2 (Distinctness.) The two parameters differ: $a_2-a_1=a_R(2/3-4/7)=a_R(14-12)/21=2a_R/21>0$, so $a_1\ne a_2$. In fact no uniqueness holds even after fixing the box: by [L1] with $a_*=a_R$, $u_1=3/2$ and $u_2=7/4$, the consistency set is the whole closed interval $[4a_R/7,2a_R/3]$, in agreement with the consistency set recorded in [F1], and every one of its elements is consistent with the record. [F1, L1, algebra]

2.1 (Conclusion.) The record $R$ is a one-point data record of the interface vocabulary with positive declared uncertainty $\varepsilon_1=1/8>0$, and steps 1.1 and 1.2 exhibit two distinct parameters of the same operational model that are both consistent with it; the uniqueness assertion of the Statement refuted is therefore false. This is an exact algebraic consistency computation on declared illustrative values: it asserts no measurement, no calibration, no probability model, no statistical inference and no empirical conclusion about the model or about any postulate. [F1, L1, step 1.1, step 1.2] ∎

## Remarks

- **Positive uncertainty is what fails to pin the parameter.** With
  $\varepsilon_1=0$ the box would be the singleton $\{5/8\}$, whose preimage
  under the strictly monotone prediction map is the single parameter
  $8a_R/13$; the failure of uniqueness in the counterexample is a property of
  the closed box of positive width together with the comparison rule, not of
  the prediction map's invertibility.

- **Scope.** The two witnesses are illustrative parameters of a hypothetical
  configuration; identifying any of them with a physical source would require
  the apparatus, calibration and analysis layer that the research queue
  records as unsupplied.

before_manifest_row.statement:
Assume Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]) and Dependent Choice ([[def-dependent-choice]]). Fix constants $c>0$, $\kappa>0$ and $\Lambda\in\mathbb R$. Let $\Sigma$ be a smooth three-manifold with smooth Riemannian metric $h$, smooth symmetric tensor $K$ and a smooth mass-normalized density $\rho_0\ge0$. Specify initial velocity as a smooth section $U_0$ of $\mathcal V=\mathbb RN\oplus T\Sigma$, with the bundle metric $g_0(aN+X,bN+Y)=-ab+h(X,Y)$, satisfying $g_0(U_0,U_0)=-1$ and positive $N$ coefficient. Thus the velocity need not be normal and does not presuppose a spacetime development. Put $\varepsilon_0=\rho_0c^2$ and require the constraints of [[thm-gr-constraint-equations-in-normal-frame]] for $T_0=\varepsilon_0U_0^{\flat_{g_0}}\otimes U_0^{\flat_{g_0}}$. On $\{\rho_0>0\}$ this is exactly the dust supplier with density parameter $\varepsilon_0$, rather than $\rho_0$ ([[def-gr-dust-matter-model]]); zero regions have independently prescribed velocity.

Then there is a smooth local development: a smooth time-oriented Lorentzian metric $g$, density $\rho\ge0$ and future unit timelike field $u$ near an embedded copy of $\Sigma$, solving
$$G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}=\kappa\rho c^2u_au_b,\qquad \nabla_uu=0,\qquad u(\rho)+\rho\nabla\!\cdot u=0.$$
The induced geometric and matter data are $(h,K,\rho_0,U_0)$, with $\mathcal V$ identified by $aN+X\mapsto an+i_*X$ using the future unit normal $n$. The initial surface lies in the interior of its domain of dependence; restriction to its Cauchy neighborhood gives a local Cauchy development. Every two such developments agree near $\Sigma$ by a data-fixing time-orientation-preserving isometry matching $\rho,u$. No division by density is used, so smooth empty regions are admitted. The neighborhood may have position-dependent time width; no uniform noncompact slab or continuation past flow crossings is asserted.

before_manifest_row.statement:
Assume Countable Choice and Dependent Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Fix $\kappa>0$, $\Lambda\in\mathbb R$ and one covariant matter model: specified smooth fields $\Psi$, equations $\mathcal E(g,\Psi)=0$ and stress expression $\mathcal T(g,\Psi)$. Pullback by local diffeomorphisms commutes with these equations and stress expression. Let $\Sigma$ be a smooth three-manifold without boundary, with smooth Riemannian metric $h$, smooth symmetric tensor $K$ and complete smooth matter Cauchy data $d$. The sign convention is $K(V,W)=g(\nabla_Vn,W)$ for the future unit normal. Initial matter tensors involving normal directions are specified on the abstract bundle $\mathcal V=\mathbb RN\oplus T\Sigma$, with metric $g_0(aN+X,bN+Y)=-ab+h(X,Y)$, rather than on a pre-existing spacetime.

before_manifest_row.title: The reciprocal ratio map $a\mapsto a_*/a$: strict decrease, inverse, and the exact preimages of points and closed intervals
before_manifest_row.statement:
## Statement

Let $a_*>0$ be a real number and define

$$F:(0,\infty)\to(0,\infty),\qquad F(a):=\frac{a_*}{a}=a_*\,a^{-1}.$$

1. **Strict decrease.** For reals $0<a_1<a_2$ one has $F(a_1)>F(a_2)$; so $F$ is
   strictly decreasing.
2. **Inverse.** $F$ is a bijection of $(0,\infty)$ onto $(0,\infty)$ with
   inverse $F^{-1}(u)=a_*/u$: that is, $F(F^{-1}(u))=u$ and
   $F^{-1}(F(a))=a$ for all $a,u>0$.
3. **Point preimages.** For every $u>0$, $F^{-1}(\{u\})=\{a_*/u\}$, and
   $F(a)=u$ holds if and only if $a=a_*/u$.
4. **Interval windows.** For reals $0<u_1\le u_2$ the preimage of the closed
   interval is

   $$F^{-1}\bigl([u_1,u_2]\bigr)=\left[\frac{a_*}{u_2},\ \frac{a_*}{u_1}\right],$$

   a nonempty closed interval contained in $(0,\infty)$, of length

   $$\frac{a_*}{u_1}-\frac{a_*}{u_2}=\frac{a_*(u_2-u_1)}{u_1u_2};$$

   the length is $0$ exactly when $u_1=u_2$ and strictly positive exactly when
   $u_1<u_2$.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** A real number $a_*>0$ and the map $F(a)=a_*a^{-1}$ on $(0,\infty)$.

[F1] $\mathbb R$ is an ordered field ([[def-ordered-field]]): the positive cone
$P=\{x\in\mathbb R:x>0\}$ is closed under multiplication, $x<y$ holds exactly
when $y-x\in P$, and for nonzero $x$ exactly one of $x\in P$, $-x\in P$ holds.
In particular $x>0$ and $y>0$ imply $xy>0$, and every nonzero real has a unique
multiplicative inverse.

[L1] Order rules ([[lem-of-sign-rules]] claims 1 and 4): if $a>0$ and $b>0$
then $ab>0$; and if $c>0$ then $a<b$ if and only if $ac<bc$.

[L2] Reciprocation ([[lem-of-inverse-positive]] claims 1 and 2): if $a>0$ then
$a^{-1}>0$; and if $0<a<b$ then $0<b^{-1}<a^{-1}$.

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 (Strict decrease.) Let $0<a_1<a_2$. By [L2] claim 2 applied to $a_1<a_2$, $0<a_2^{-1}<a_1^{-1}$; since $a_*>0$, [L1] claim 4 (multiplying the strict inequality by the positive number $a_*$) gives $a_*a_2^{-1}<a_*a_1^{-1}$, that is, $F(a_2)<F(a_1)$ by the definition of $F$. Hence $F$ is strictly decreasing on $(0,\infty)$, which is claim 1. [F1, L1, L2, algebra]

1.2 (Inverse and bijectivity.) Let $u>0$. By [L2] claim 1, $a_*/u>0$, so $a_*/u$ lies in the domain $(0,\infty)$ of $F$ and is nonzero; using associativity, commutativity and the inverse law in the field $\mathbb R$ ([F1]), $F\bigl(F^{-1}(u)\bigr)=a_*(a_*/u)^{-1}=a_*\,u\,a_*^{-1}=u$. Symmetrically, for $a>0$ one has $F^{-1}\bigl(F(a)\bigr)=a_*(a_*a^{-1})^{-1}=a_*\,a\,a_*^{-1}=a$. Thus $F$ and the map $u\mapsto a_*/u$ are mutually inverse, so $F$ is a bijection of $(0,\infty)$ onto $(0,\infty)$; this is claim 2. [F1, L2, algebra]

1.3 (Interval windows.) Let $0<u_1\le u_2$ and $a>0$. The inequality $F(a)\in[u_1,u_2]$ reads $u_1\le a_*a^{-1}\le u_2$; multiplying both inequalities by the positive number $a$ via [L1] claim 4 gives $u_1a\le a_*\le u_2a$, equivalently $u_1a\le a_*$ and $a_*\le u_2a$. Dividing the first inequality by the positive $u_1$ and the second by the positive $u_2$, again by [L1] claim 4, gives $a\le a_*/u_1$ and $a\ge a_*/u_2$, that is, $a\in[a_*/u_2,\,a_*/u_1]$. Conversely every $a$ in that interval satisfies $u_1a\le a_*\le u_2a$ and hence, after division by the positive $a$, lies in $F^{-1}([u_1,u_2])$; so $F^{-1}([u_1,u_2])=[a_*/u_2,a_*/u_1]$. The interval is nonempty because $u_1\le u_2$ and division of positive numbers reverses the reciprocal order ([L2] claim 2 applied to $u_1<u_2$, with the equality case $u_1=u_2$ giving coincident endpoints), and both endpoints are strictly positive by [L2] claim 1; this is the first part of claim 4. [F1, L1, L2, algebra]

2.1 (Point preimages.) Let $u>0$ and $a>0$. Multiplying the equation $a_*a^{-1}=u$ by the nonzero number $a$ and using field arithmetic gives $a_*=ua$; multiplying instead by the nonzero number $u^{-1}$ gives $a=a_*u^{-1}=a_*/u$. Conversely $F(a_*/u)=u$ by step 1.2. Hence $F(a)=u$ if and only if $a=a_*/u$, and the point preimage is the singleton $\{a_*/u\}$; this is claim 3. [F1, L1, L2, step 1.2, algebra]

2.2 (Length of the window.) The length of the interval of step 1.3 is $\frac{a_*}{u_1}-\frac{a_*}{u_2}=\frac{a_*u_2-a_*u_1}{u_1u_2}=\frac{a_*(u_2-u_1)}{u_1u_2}$, by field arithmetic. The denominator is a product of positive numbers, hence positive ([F1], [L1] claim 1), and the numerator is a product of $a_*>0$ with $u_2-u_1\ge0$, hence nonnegative, and positive exactly when $u_2-u_1>0$ by the trichotomy in [F1]. Therefore the length is zero exactly when $u_1=u_2$ and strictly positive exactly when $u_1<u_2$, which completes claim 4. [F1, L1, L2, step 1.3, algebra]

3.1 Collecting the steps: claim 1 is step 1.1, claim 2 is step 1.2, claim 3 is step 2.1, and claim 4 is steps 1.3 and 2.2. No step uses calculus, a choice principle, a limit or a completeness property of $\mathbb R$ beyond the ordered field axioms of [F1]; the map and its inverse are explicit rational expressions. [F1, step 1.1, step 1.2, step 2.1, step 1.3, step 2.2] ∎
